scale.uncertainty: Do not confuseH/h with wall thickness. Approximate axial thickness8–12mm is acceptable without claiming anatomical calibration; diameter about55mm. Original body was not a flat2D extrusion.

morphology: Continuous essentially planar open coil. Fine early nucleus remains tight, then successive later whorls separate naturally with a conspicuous open interval, followingFig2. Do not turn it into a normal involute disk, disconnected concentric rings, helix, shaft or terminal hook.

Outer coil grows only slowly in tube height and opens widely after diameter30–35mm; inner growth differs from outer. Do not impose one uniform logarithmic growth parameter that closes the actual open gap. Trace the actual variable spiral silhouette.

Last preserved tube has about12mm radial height at55mm overall diameter. Cross-section inferred as mildly elliptical with rounded ventral/flank surfaces and flatter dorsal/inner surface, not a rectangular strip, perfect hose or razor-thin extrusion.
Preserved outer terminal end is upper-right inPlate36fig2, with a blunt irregular mineral-filled face. No unsupported extension completing another turn, no polished hollow aperture or living tissue.

Many fine transverse ribs follow the changing local tube direction. Earlier main ribs bear small ventrolateral spine remnants with3–4 finer non-tuberculate ribs between; mature ribs become similar in strength and spines fade. Keep subdued and varying, not identical washer rings.
Visible short spine remnants are concentrated on the intermediate coil. Preserve low irregular projections, not a symmetrical forest of giant spikes or long reconstructed missing spines.
Centre and turns are one continuous growing shell. Keep the genuine interwhorl opening; no support struts, stone slab, pedestal or labels spanning the negative spaces.
Material neutral matte fossil stone. No live animal, cutaway septa, rainbow ammolite, copied photo texture, museum sticker or numerical markings.
uncertainty: Only one lateral image exists in the selected source; axial thickness, backside and fine three-dimensional rib shape are conservatively inferred from published section description, not observed in independent angles.
WidthW is explicitly not reported. Maker must not write9mm as measured holotype width or certify a photogrammetric replica.
Unpreserved early micro-whorls and terminal shell beyond the fossil are not restored. Preserved morphology remains sufficient to express original natural open planar spiral.
Later taxonomic changes were not identified in the sources checked; use2010 primary identification and its specimen number rather than C.nolani or an unverified dealer specimen.
palette: Matte warm-grey stone, at most subtle variation at worn terminal face; artistic choice.
acceptance_focus: Front: matchPl36fig2 natural open coil, tight earliest part and broad later gap; terminal upper-right.
Side/top: visible but restrained elliptical thickness and planar centreline, no helical displacement or sheet extrusion.
Perspective: continuous connected coil, no fused later turns, no fake drilled hole or shaft/hook.
